title: Compact Fidelity Handshake Language (CFHL) — SDK PRD
content:
Purpose:
This PRD proposes a compact fidelity handshake language (CFHL) — a small, deterministic, versioned protocol that SDKs and the Hosted API runtime use to: (1) negotiate how much and which parts of an LLM response are delivered progressively, (2) express tool-call expectations and fallbacks in a machine-readable way, and (3) carry structured-output hints that improve client ergonomics and reduce surface area for ad-hoc heuristics. The goal is predictable client behavior across network conditions and product tiers while keeping the wire format minimal for mobile and embedded use-cases.

Problem statement:
- Clients and SDKs currently implement many ad-hoc heuristics for partial responses, tool-call handshakes, and fallback strategies. This leads to fragile client logic, duplicated feature work, and discrepancies between SDKs and server behavior (esp. in low-bandwidth / intermittent networks).
- Streaming payloads can include mixed fidelity: a quick summary, then detail, then structured objects for downstream parsing. Without a common negotiation language, clients either over-fetch (higher cost/latency) or under-handle (lost functionality).

Goals (product + engineering):
- Define a compact, text-first handshake envelope (CFHL v1) that fits easily into existing streaming frames and is small enough for low-bandwidth clients.
- Surface a small set of fidelity operators (e.g., preview, body, authoritative-structured, tool-proxy) clients can request and servers honor or map to fallbacks.
- Include explicit tool-call metadata (expected tool schema, call-liveness hints, optional lease TTL) so SDKs can manage tool proxies and offline retries deterministically.
- Provide clear backward compatibility rules and upgrade path for older SDKs/servers.
- Instrument telemetry hooks and SLO targets to validate utility and detect mismatch patterns.

Non-goals:
- Not proposing a full binary framing protocol — CFHL is intentionally human-readable and small.
- Not aiming to fully replace all existing streaming frames; CFHL should co-exist with current incremental output format until adoption.

CFHL v1 (proposal summary):
- Placement: CFHL is a small JSONL line prefixed with an agreed token ("cfhl:\") that can be emitted as an early frame and as in-band metadata for subsequent frames. Example: cfhl:{"ver":"1","req_fidelity":["preview","authoritative-structured"],"tool_expect":[{"name":"search","schema":"/schemas/search-v2","lease":30}],"resume_token":"tkn_..."}
- Fidelity operators (canonical set):
  - preview: short, low-cost summary tokens suitable for immediate UX.
  - body: the full free-text generation stream.
  - authoritative-structured: server-provided structured data (JSON objects) intended for machine consumption with explicit schema reference.
  - tool-proxy: signals that a tool will be invoked and the client should expect either a tool-result frame or a fallback narrative.
- Fallback mapping: server will include a fallback map when a requested fidelity cannot be satisfied: {"preview":"body-first","authoritative-structured":"body-with-annotations"}. SDKs interpret mapping rules to present deterministic UIs.
- Tool call hints: name, canonical schema URI, min_expected_latency_ms, lease_seconds (optional). SDKs use lease_seconds to manage ephemeral local caches and to decide whether to block UI for a tool result or show best-effort content.
- Resume semantics: CFHL supports a resume_token that SDKs persist to re-request the remainder of a partial stream; server may accept resume tokens for a configurable TTL.

SDK ergonomics / developer flows:
- Default client policy: if preview is present, render immediately; if tool-proxy exists and lease_seconds <= 5, render preview and block until tool result arrives; if lease_seconds > 5 show preview and attach tool-result when available.
- Typed bindings: SDKs expose a small runtime (CFHLClient) that parses cfhl: frames and emits typed events: onPreview, onBodyChunk, onStructured(schemaUri, object), onToolLeaseStart, onToolResult.
- Backoff & retry: resume_token allows SDK to re-open a paused stream; SDKs should implement exponential backoff with jitter for resume attempts and surface a final state to app (complete, partial, resumed_rejected).

Observability & telemetry:
- Emit telemetry keys for: negotiated_fidelities, fallback_used, tool_lease_duration, resume_attempts, resume_success.
- Add dashboard in Console per-route: %streams using CFHL, %requests that negotiated authoritative-structured, median tool-lease observed, distribution of fallback types.
- Alert: >5% fallback rate for a model-route pair for 24h -> triage configuration/quantization or model mismatch.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Server-side: implement CFHL v1 emitter that can be toggled per-route. When disabled server emits a minimal compatibility frame: cfhl:{"ver":"0"} to indicate legacy behavior.
- SDKs: release CFHL-aware 1.x SDKs that parse v1 frames and implement default UX policy. 1.x should tolerate ver:"0" and fall back to current ad-hoc heuristics.
- Gradual rollout: opt-in beta on 10% of traffic for 2 weeks; collect telemetry, iterate on operator names and mappings. Expand to 50% after fixes, then flip default.

Acceptance criteria (for v1 GA):
- SDKs (JS, Python, iOS, Android) correctly parse CFHL frames and emit typed events in integration tests.
- Telemetry shows <1% stream parse errors across rollouts and <10% unexpected fallback mapping for beta traffic.
- Developer docs + one quickstart (React native chat sample) available.

Open questions / risks:
- Should CFHL use a binary prefix (msgpack) for even smaller size? (trade-off: mobile debugger friendliness).
- Lease semantics across multi-region failover — server must ensure lease monotonicity; potential complexity.
- Schema discovery and trust model for authoritative-structured payloads (embedding a schema URI implies server-hosted spec; we need signing/versioning).

Next milestones:
- Week 0-2: internal RFC + integration test harness (serving-runtime + JS SDK)
- Week 3-5: beta toggle and 10% traffic pilot (collect telemetry)
- Week 6-8: SDK coverage for Python/iOS/Android + docs and quickstarts
- Week 9-10: 50% expansion + stability hardening
- Week 12: GA flip and postmortem instrumentation

Appendix: quick CFHL example stream (text with cfhl lines):
cfhl:{"ver":"1","req_fidelity":["preview","authoritative-structured"],"tool_expect":[{"name":"kb_lookup","schema":"/schemas/kb-v1"}],"resume_token":"r_abc"}
<frame>preview text tokens</frame>
cfhl:{"phase":"tool-proxy","tool":"kb_lookup","lease":8}
<frame>body tokens...</frame>
cfhl:{"phase":"structured","schema":"/schemas/kb-v1","payload":"<base64-json>..."}

If this approach looks reasonable we should spin up an RFC in github and start a small UX prototype with the React SDK to validate default policies and size characteristics on cellular networks.
